meta.disclaimer: Figures combine confirmed disclosures with analyst estimates. Check confidence and sources per project before use. Rows with isDemoData=true are illustrative seed data and must not be used in analysis.

projects.name: AWS Madison County
projects.analystNotes: Two campuses across ~1,700 acres. Capex is Madison County only: the original $10B (Jan 2024) plus the $11B expansion (Apr 2026). Amazon's total Mississippi commitment is $25B including other sites. No MW disclosed.

projects.name: AWS Mexico (Central) Region — Querétaro
projects.analystNotes: $5B is a 15-year commitment across three Querétaro data centers, not a single-site capex; AWS projects ~$10B GDP contribution and ~7,000 jobs. Region live since Jan 14, 2025 with AI/ML services framing; MW never disclosed. Querétaro also hosts Google and Microsoft regions — Mexico's datacenter epicenter, with drought/water scrutiny.

projects.name: AWS Richmond County
projects.analystNotes: ~800 acres, ~20 planned buildings, adjacent to Duke Energy's Smith Energy Complex. Largest single capital project in North Carolina history; broke ground July 2026. No MW disclosed.

projects.name: AWS Salem Township
projects.analystNotes: Former Talen Cumulus campus adjacent to the Susquehanna nuclear plant, bought for $650M in Mar 2024 with ~240 MW developed at acquisition; ramping toward up to 960 MW site power. The 2025 Talen PPA covers up to 1,920 MW across AWS Pennsylvania sites. No source states the currently energized level, so nothing is recorded as confirmed.

projects.name: Abilene Clean Campus (Crusoe)
projects.description: Crusoe-developed capacity adjacent to Stargate Abilene, reported at roughly 900 MW after OpenAI declined the expansion.
projects.analystNotes: Tenancy is unsettled: OpenAI declined the expansion and Microsoft is reported to be in talks. Recorded as unattributed capacity rather than assigned to a tenant that has not signed.

projects.name: AirTrunk SYD3
projects.analystNotes: AirTrunk (Blackstone) lists SYD3 at 330 MW+; industry trackers cite a >400 MW master plan. Serves hyperscale cloud/AI customers; anchor tenants not officially disclosed. Full campus not energized.

projects.name: Aligned Project Caprock
projects.analystNotes: Capex null: release says 'The site is expected to infuse $5B into the regional economy' — regional economic impact, not stated construction capex. First data center LBB-01 'anticipated service date of Q1 2027.' Closed-loop cooling avoiding Ogallala Aquifer draw. Same county as the covered Fluidstack/Anthropic Abernathy campus but a separate project. Aligned itself was acquired in a ~$40B deal by the MGX/BlackRock-GIP AI Infrastructure Partnership (Oct 2025).

projects.name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1
projects.analystNotes: Capex null per rules: the headline '$11B' is contracted lease revenue ('brings Applied Digital's total anticipated contracted lease revenue to approximately $11B'), not construction capex. 400MW is critical IT load (leases ~15 years, first two signed May-June 2025). Applied Digital is also developing Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND). First 50MW came online 2025; Building 1 Phase 1 ready-for-service achieved for CoreWeave.

projects.name: Bell AI Fabric — Kamloops
projects.analystNotes: 500MW six-site target is ambition, not committed capacity: first 7MW Groq-equipped Kamloops site live June 2025, 7MW Merritt site and 26MW Thompson Rivers University facility (2026) plus second 26MW Kamloops facility (2027) committed; two further ~400MW-combined sites only 'in advanced planning'. Bloomberg reported (2026-06-18) BCE teaming with Cohere on a Canada AI data center, and (2026-03-16) CoreWeave/BCE backing a large western-Canada facility — expansion of this fabric.

projects.name: ByteDance Johor
projects.analystNotes: Capex is the June 2024 RM10B (~$2.13B) AI-hub commitment; Johor officials put cumulative ByteDance datacenter investment above RM29.5B (~$6.6B) by Jan 2026, spread across own-build and leased capacity. Existing Sedenak facility operating, expansion ongoing. No site MW disclosed.

projects.name: ByteDance Pecém Campus

location.city: Caucaia / São Gonçalo do Amarante (Pecém port complex)

projects.analystNotes: ByteDance's largest datacenter outside China; R$200B (~US$38.4B) lifetime figure is the full multi-phase ambition — initial build is ~200MW IT (20 halls), with reported scaling to ~900MW-1GW by 2029. First reported by Reuters late 2025; construction began Jan 2026 (only pillars erected as of July 2026). Omnia (Pátria) signed a US$2B, 20-year wind PPA with Casa dos Ventos (630MW Ibiapaba complex). Local grid-strain scrutiny in Ceará. Capex omitted on review: the R$200B (~US$38.4B) figure is the full multi-phase lifetime ambition, not committed phase-one spend.

projects.name: Campus IA Fouju
projects.analystNotes:
UAE-backed JV of MGX, Bpifrance, Mistral AI and NVIDIA, announced at Choose France 2025; site fixed at ZAC des Bordes, Fouju. Public inquiry under way per the prefecture (hence PERMITTING); construction planned from H2 2026, operations by 2028. Reported ~€8.5B initial investment not captured from a primary source, so no capex recorded.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: a French Senate question record (May 2026) confirms the 1.4 GW target and the public inquiry (open 30 April–30 May 2026), and states that only 700 MW has so far been contracted with grid operator RTE — half the headline figure. MGX holds a majority of the capital.

projects.name: Cassava Cape Town
projects.analystNotes: Africa's first NVIDIA-powered 'AI factory', live March 2026 inside existing Africa Data Centres facilities — GPU-as-a-service, not a new-build campus, so no MW is recorded. The 12,000-GPU figure is a continent-wide acquisition claim, initial SA deployment reported around 3,000; neither is confirmed, so no GPU count is recorded. Johannesburg expansion planned.

projects.name: China Telecom Lingang intelligent computing center
projects.analystNotes: 40,000 high-power racks planned in Lingang free-trade zone, mainly serving home-grown GPU development for Shanghai/Yangtze Delta AI firms. Per-site rack figure, no MW disclosed. Context: China Telecom is China's largest AIDC operator (900+ DCs, ~8GW total per company statements — aggregate, not this site).

projects.name: China Telecom Shaoguan
projects.analystNotes: Shaoguan is a Greater Bay Area national hub node under East Data West Computing. China Telecom owns/operates the facility; Alibaba supplies Zhenwu 810E accelerators (96GB HBM2e, T-Head architecture). Companies say the cluster is expected to expand to 100,000 chips; that expansion figure is a plan, not installed capacity.

projects.name: Cipher Black Pearl
projects.analystNotes: Capex null: '~$5.5Bn Estimated Contract Value' is 15-year lease revenue, not construction capex. 300MW is gross power (site energized as front-of-the-meter bitcoin campus; Phase I 150MW mined BTC from Q2 2025). AWS also later revealed as tenant at Cipher's Stingray site ('a 70 MW critical IT load'). Cipher's separate Barber Lake site (244MW gross/168MW IT) is leased to Fluidstack with a $1.4B Google backstop, and its 1GW Colchis site is expected to energize in 2028.

projects.name: CloudHQ Paulínia (GRU) Campus
projects.analystNotes: CloudHQ's first Latin America campus; press reports cite '$3.2B' but the sourced quote says 'more than $3 billion' — capex recorded at $3B floor. 225MW substation (expandable toward 400MW) energized; hyperscale AI/cloud tenants targeted. Roughly 100km from São Paulo metro.

projects.name: CloudHQ QRO Campus Querétaro
projects.analystNotes: CloudHQ's largest single investment: six AI-oriented buildings (~US$800M each) on ~52ha, 900MW private substation + 2GW maneuvering substation, water-free cooling, LEED targets. Infrastructure delivery/first operations targeted 2027; ~7,000 construction jobs. Would be Mexico's largest hyperscale hub.

projects.name: Compass Meridian
projects.analystNotes: 'The campus will consist of eight data centers that will be constructed over an eight-year period.' Compass leases build-to-suit to investment-grade hyperscalers; end tenant not officially disclosed (Meta widely speculated in trade press, unconfirmed). 500MW figure is utility supply (site power), not critical IT load. 10-year state tax exemptions granted.

projects.name: Core Scientific Denton
projects.analystNotes: CoreWeave's largest contracted Core Scientific site (~260 MW critical IT load; 590 MW across six sites in the relationship, full delivery targeted early 2027). Converted bitcoin-mining site. The $1.2B figure is contracted hosting revenue, not capex, so no capex is recorded.

projects.name: CoreWeave Cambridge
projects.analystNotes: First investment under Canada's C$2B Sovereign AI Compute Strategy: up to C$240M federal financing toward Cohere's C$725M compute plan (figures in CAD, hence capexUsd null). CoreWeave operates the Cambridge facility, opened mid-2025; MW capacity undisclosed. Cohere has since also sourced Canadian compute via Bell's sovereign AI alliance (The Logic/Bloomberg, June 2026).

projects.name: CoreWeave Lancaster
projects.analystNotes: Initial 100 MW expandable to 300 MW. Capex is CoreWeave's stated 'up to $6 billion' commitment.

projects.name: Crusoe Goodnight
projects.analystNotes: Part of Google's November 2025 plan to 'invest $40 billion in Texas data centers' (Armstrong and Haskell counties) — capex null because $40B spans multiple sites. 'In January 2026, Crusoe filed a permit to build a 933 MW natural gas power plant onsite'; satellite imagery confirms two buildings under construction; first phase shares interconnection with a wind farm, segment due online in 2026. Third-party trackers list full build at ~1,030MW / 7 buildings / 3.4M sq ft. Distinct from Crusoe's covered Abilene (Stargate) campus and from Crusoe-Lancium's separately announced 1GW Childress partnership.

projects.name: CyrusOne Freestone
projects.analystNotes: CyrusOne's largest single announced US AI campus; brings Constellation/Calpine-contracted CyrusOne capacity in Texas to 'a total of over 1100 MW under contract' including the earlier 400MW Whitney/Bosque County campus (DFW10, first building topped out March 2026) at Calpine's Thad Hill Energy Center. No online date disclosed.

projects.name: DT Industrial AI Cloud
projects.analystNotes: Opened February 2026 in a renovated Munich Tucherpark datacenter; ~€1B privately financed with NVIDIA. GPU count is DT's stated 'up to 10,000' ceiling (1,000+ DGX B200 systems). Facility MW not disclosed. Anchor customers reported include Mercedes-Benz, Siemens and BMW.

projects.name: DataVolt Oxagon
projects.analystNotes: 1.5 GW total campus target, basis unstated; capex of $5B covers phase one only, with the first ~300 MW targeted for 2028. NEOM megaprojects have a documented history of rescoping and no construction on this campus is documented as of mid-2026 — treat scale as aspirational.

projects.name: EcoCloud Olkaria
projects.analystNotes: Geothermal-powered campus with Microsoft as cloud partner (~$1B initial investment announced May 2024). Recorded at the 100 MW initial phase, not the 1 GW ceiling. Per May 2026 reporting the plan has stalled — the commissioning date was abandoned and government approval never materialized — hence PAUSED. A smaller ~60 MW KenGen-led project continues separately.

projects.name: Edged–Merlin Extremadura
projects.analystNotes: Two campuses (Navalmoral de la Mata and Valdecaballeros) of up to 1 GW IT each, recorded as one combined 2 GW row matching the partners' joint announcement. Public–private with the regional government; no construction, tenant, capex or timeline confirmed — aspirational scale.

projects.name: Fir Hills Jeollanam-do

location.city: Jeollanam-do (site not finalized in cited reports)

projects.analystNotes: Claimed 3GW / ~$35bn (KRW 50tn) campus by Brian Koo's Stock Farm Road vehicle Fir Hills, in partnership with Jeollanam-do provincial government; construction targeted from winter 2025, completion 2028. DCD framing ('claims') reflects skepticism; as of 2026 the project remains in pre-construction/structuring. Sometimes reported alongside a Jeonju (North Jeolla) proposal — cited sources place this project in Jeollanam-do. 3GW is planned capacity, basis not broken out. Status RUMORED on review: DCD frames the project as a claim and no construction is documented.

projects.name: Firmus Batam AI Factory
projects.analystNotes: Co-developed with DayOne; NVIDIA compute partnership through 2034, GPU deliveries through 2027–28. The cited $25–30B is committed offtake revenue, not capex. First operations targeted Q1 2027. GPU count is the announced deployment ceiling ('up to 170,000').

projects.name: Fluidstack Abernathy
projects.analystNotes: Originally a TeraWulf–Fluidstack 51/49 JV (Google-backed); in July 2026 TeraWulf sold its stake to a Fluidstack-led group. 168 MW critical IT / 240 MW gross site power. Delivery expected H2 2026. Widely reported as the Texas site of Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program.

projects.name: Foxconn Kaohsiung AI Factory
projects.analystNotes: National AI factory with NVIDIA, TSMC and Taiwan's NSTC; phased 20→60→100 MW due to grid constraints, full deployment targeted 2026. Phase-1 energization not independently confirmed.

projects.name: Galaxy Helios
projects.analystNotes: Former bitcoin mine on 2,200+ acres; gross vs IT explicitly distinguished by Galaxy ('approximately 200 megawatts of gross power — 133 MW of critical IT load'). 15-year CoreWeave lease 'expected to generate more than $1 billion in average annual revenue' — lease revenue, not capex, hence capexUsd null. Phase I rent commenced Q2 2026. First CoreWeave lease announced March 2025 (month precision).

projects.name: Google Cedar Rapids
projects.analystNotes: Google's second Iowa campus at Alliant Energy's Big Cedar Industrial Center; first building projected complete 2026, four more in later phases. $7B is statewide over two years, so no campus-level capex is recorded. No MW disclosed.

projects.name: Google Cerrillos
projects.analystNotes: Cautionary status entry: 2020-permitted ~US$200M (reported) project abandoned in original form after Chile's Second Environmental Court partially revoked its permit over aquifer/water use (Feb 2024); Google committed to restart permitting 'from scratch' with air cooling and 24/7 carbon-free energy. No new approval as of mid-2026. Google's operational Chilean site remains Quilicura.

projects.name: Google Stillwater
projects.analystNotes: New AI-focused campus on ~400 acres, phase one targeted 2027. The $9B figure is statewide (also expands the existing Pryor campus), so no campus-level capex is recorded. No MW disclosed.

projects.name: Google Visakhapatnam
projects.analystNotes: Google's largest AI hub outside the US; $15B over 2026–2030 includes subsea cable gateway and clean energy. Foundation laid April 2026. 1 GW is 'compute capacity' with basis unstated. Partners AdaniConneX and Nxtra.

projects.name: Google West Memphis
projects.analystNotes: ~1,000-acre site powered by Entergy Arkansas; construction began Oct 2025 on an 18–24 month build. $4B through 2027 is the company-stated figure; local bond filings suggest the ultimate buildout could be far larger. No MW disclosed.

projects.name: HUMAIN AI Factories Phase 1
projects.analystNotes: PIF-backed sovereign program. 200 MW covers the two under-construction launch sites (up to 100 MW each, Riyadh and Dammam), basis unstated. The 500 MW NVIDIA target, a separate 500 MW AMD collaboration and the up-to-6 GW-by-2034 ambition are aspirational and not recorded as capacity. No source confirms energization as of late July 2026.

projects.name: HUMAIN–xAI Data Center
projects.analystNotes: Announced at the US–Saudi investment forum; described as xAI's largest datacenter outside the US, for Grok training. Exact site, timeline and phasing undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded. No construction documented as of July 2026.

projects.name: Hut 8 River Bend
projects.analystNotes: $7.0B is lease contract value (revenue, not capex); the $10B figure is LED's stated Phase I project investment. 'Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., is providing a financial backstop'; Fluidstack holds 'a Right of First Offer (ROFO) for up to an additional 1,000 MW of IT capacity.' Entergy providing '330 MW of utility capacity for the campus.' Initial data hall 'scheduled for completion and commissioning in Q2 2027.' Financed partly via $3.25B bond sale. Hut 8's GPU vertical operates as Highrise AI.

projects.name: IREN Childress
projects.analystNotes: '750 MW campus located in Childress, Texas.' $9.7B is contract value (cloud services revenue), not capex — capexUsd null; hardware funded partly via '$5.8 billion' Dell purchase agreement and a 20% Microsoft prepayment. Site began as grid-connected bitcoin campus (345kV). Horizon 1 (first GB300 cluster) handover targeted Q3 2026.

projects.name: IREN Sweetwater
projects.analystNotes: Energization is the high-voltage substation connection to ERCOT, not operating IT capacity: 'Power delivery at Sweetwater 1 is expected to ramp progressively in line with the phased construction and commissioning of data centers.' Sweetwater 2 (600MW, ~28 miles away) targeted late 2027; the two sites are to be fiber-linked into a single 2GW hub. Coordinates approximate (town of Sweetwater).

projects.name: Isambard-AI
projects.analystNotes: UK's most powerful supercomputer, fully launched July 2025, serving the UK AI Research Resource; 5,448 GH200 superchips. The 5 MW figure describes the operating facility, stated by the operator, hence recorded as confirmed. Capex converts the quoted £225M.

projects.name: JUPITER
projects.analystNotes: Europe's first exascale system, inaugurated September 2025 and in operation; funded 50% EuroHPC JU, 50% German federal/NRW. Capex includes six years of operations. A ~18 MW power figure circulates from TOP500 data but no quotable source was captured, so no MW is recorded.

projects.name: KDDI Osaka Sakai
projects.analystNotes:
Opened 2026-01-22 on part of Sharp's former Sakai LCD plant (KDDI bought its parcel for ~JPY10bn/US$68m in April 2025; GB200 NVL72 racks, direct liquid cooling, 100% renewable power). Distinct from SoftBank's separate 150MW project on the larger portion of the same Sharp Sakai site (already covered). 48MW is facility capacity as reported at launch; IT-vs-total basis not broken out.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: operations since 2026-01-22 are primary-sourced (KDDI), but the 48 MW figure appears only in trade press and describes facility capacity, not critical IT load. Reclassified from confirmed operating to an estimate accordingly.

projects.name: Khazna UAE Expansion
projects.analystNotes: Part of Microsoft's $15.2B UAE commitment through 2029 (country-wide figure, so no capex recorded here). Khazna groundbreakings in Abu Dhabi support under-construction status; specific sites for the full 200 MW not disclosed. Distinct from Stargate UAE.

projects.name: Lambda Kansas City
projects.analystNotes: Retrofit of a vacant facility; $500M per Missouri economic-development reporting. 24 MW at launch, potential to scale past 100 MW; energization not publicly confirmed as of July 2026. Announcement date approximate (Nov 2025).

projects.name: Meta El Paso
projects.analystNotes: Broke ground Oct 2025. On 2026-07-28 Meta and BlackRock (with GIP and HPS) announced a JV owning the campus — BlackRock funds 80%, Meta 20%, ~$14B total development cost. Capacity online from 2028. Reported to rely partly on on-site natural gas generation.

projects.name: Meta Hyperion
projects.description: Multi-gigawatt AI training campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana — the largest single-site build publicly announced.
projects.analystNotes:
5 GW is a full-build target across many phases, not near-term capacity. Treated as an estimate; no phase is confirmed energised in the sources reviewed.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: Meta's July 13, 2026 announcement formally expanded Hyperion to 5 GW and more than $50B (from 2 GW/~$27B). Committed phase: 2 GW by 2030; full build reported ~2032. Nothing is operating yet — Epoch projects 1,676 MW IT by Q1 2028.

projects.name: Meta Lebanon
projects.analystNotes: Groundbreaking 2026-02-11; Meta's 27th US data center. Reported full operation late 2027/early 2028, recorded as no date since sources give a range. 1 GW basis (IT vs site) not specified.

projects.name: Meta Prometheus
projects.description: New Albany, Ohio campus targeting 1 GW, with nuclear supply agreements signed in January 2026.
projects.analystNotes:
Nuclear agreements with TerraPower, Oklo and Vistra are power-purchase commitments, not on-site reactors delivering today.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: Epoch lists Prometheus operational at an estimated 631 MW IT (854 MW projected by Q4 2026) against the ~1 GW announced cluster scale. Status moved to partially operational; the 1 GW figure remains the announced nameplate. Not operator-confirmed capacity, so nothing enters the confirmed column.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater — Atlanta
projects.description: Atlanta campus paired with the Wisconsin Fairwater site over dedicated fibre to operate as one distributed training system.
projects.analystNotes:
Paired with the Wisconsin site; the two are reported to operate as a single distributed training fabric.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: the 350 MW figure was the building-1 floor at the November 2025 launch. Epoch now estimates 636 MW IT with buildings 3 and 4 operational by June 2026. Microsoft's own materials still state no megawatt figure, so this is an analyst estimate, not confirmed capacity.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater — Wisconsin
projects.description: Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin site, reported live June 2026, linked by dedicated fibre to the Atlanta Fairwater campus.
projects.analystNotes:
Closed-loop liquid cooling, reported to eliminate operational water consumption. Reported as exceeding 350 MW and scaling further, so 350 MW is a floor rather than a point estimate.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: Microsoft announced completion of the first Mount Pleasant facility on 2026-06-23 ('now fully operational'). Epoch estimates 369 MW IT currently, projecting 2,263 MW by Q2 2028 with the second facility (2028); Microsoft has separately proposed two further Mount Pleasant campuses (~$13.3B, ~2 GW). No operator megawatt figure exists, so the capacity stays an estimate.

projects.name: Microsoft Hyderabad
projects.analystNotes: Flagship of Microsoft's $17.5B 2026–2029 India commitment (country-wide figure, so no site capex recorded). Three availability zones; targeted live mid-2026. No site MW disclosed.

projects.name: Microsoft Pecos
projects.analystNotes: Reeves County, West Texas. ~2 GW served by a co-located behind-the-meter natural gas facility; 'multibillion-dollar' investment over five to seven years, no specific capex stated. Basis (IT vs site) not stated. Distinct from the Fairwater sites.

projects.name: NAVER GAK Sejong AI Factory
projects.description: Sovereign AI factory at NAVER's GAK Sejong hyperscale data centre, announced 25 July 2026 for expansion to 200 MW by 2028 with Brookfield as exclusive capital partner.
projects.analystNotes:
NAVER states a long-term ambition to reach 1 GW of NVIDIA AI infrastructure. That is an intent, not a committed build, and is deliberately NOT counted in the capacity figures — only the announced 200 MW by 2028 is. Funding split: Brookfield up to $9B as exclusive capital partner, NVIDIA $1B, NAVER the remainder.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: the NVIDIA/NAVER/Brookfield announcement (2026-07-24) is explicit that the DSX buildout expands 'from 55 megawatts to 200 megawatts by 2028'. The row previously carried the 2028 target as if current; it now records 55 MW, with 200 MW by 2028 and a stated 1 GW long-term intent held as targets.

projects.name: Nebius Béthune
projects.analystNotes: Redevelopment of a former Bridgestone tyre plant near Lille. Reuters: first capacity online by late summer 2026 and roughly half the site operational by end of 2026. Nebius did not disclose cost; third-party estimates are excluded.

projects.name: Nebius Highridge
projects.analystNotes: Nebius's second US gigawatt-scale campus, Schuylkill County; ~3-year build, still in local approvals as of July 2026. 1.2 GW is grid supply from PPL (site power, not stated as IT load).

projects.name: Nebius Lappeenranta AI Factory
projects.analystNotes: Nebius's largest facility outside the US, on a ~100-acre industrial site. Press reports value the project above $10B but that is not in the primary release, so no capex is recorded. Distinct from Nebius's operational Mäntsälä site.

projects.name: Nebius Vineland
projects.analystNotes: Phased development to 300 MW design capacity (basis not stated as IT load). Anchor for Nebius's ~$17.4B Microsoft dedicated-capacity agreement; first phases energized, full 300 MW not confirmed operating.

projects.name: Nexus AI Factory Morocco
projects.analystNotes: Consortium with NAVER, NVIDIA and Lloyd Capital; first phase 40 MW with GB200s, staged toward a 500 MW target; renewable supply via TAQA. Construction start not independently confirmed, so ANNOUNCED. Would be among Africa's largest AI facilities.

projects.name: Nscale Barstow
projects.analystNotes: Site leased from Ionic Digital; fourth Nscale–Microsoft deal, reported at up to $24B (contract value, not capex). Construction from Q3 2026; Microsoft holds an option for a further 700 MW from Q1 2027. 240 MW initial, expandable to 1.2 GW; basis unstated. GPU count is the announced deployment plan.

projects.name: Nscale Loughton
projects.analystNotes: Billed as the UK's largest AI supercomputer when live, serving Microsoft Azure. 90 MW is the scalable ceiling (50 MW initial). GPU count is the announced initial deployment for Q1 2027. Part of Nscale's ~200,000-GB300 Microsoft contract across Europe and the US.

projects.name: Ooredoo Sovereign AI Cloud
projects.analystNotes: First NVIDIA Cloud Partner sovereign AI cloud in Qatar, live since ~July 2025 in existing Ooredoo/Syntys facilities. Dedicated MW and GPU count undisclosed, so no figures are recorded. Syntys's >120 MW / ~$1B plan is a group datacenter target, not this deployment.

projects.name: OpenAI–Tata HyperVault
projects.analystNotes: OpenAI is the first customer of TCS's HyperVault data-center business: 100 MW initially, with plans to scale to 1 GW. Site undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded. Part of Stargate per OpenAI.

projects.name: Poolside Project Horizon
projects.analystNotes:
2GW campus on 568 acres of the Mitchell family's Longfellow Ranch, gas-rich Permian Basin site. CoreWeave was anchor tenant (15-yr lease, 250MW first phase expandable to 500MW, planned 40,000+ GB300 NVL72 GPUs) but the deal was mutually terminated in early 2026; Poolside approached other clouds incl. Google ('Google is no longer in talks with Poolside'). Power figure is planned gross site power, none operating.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: the CoreWeave anchor lease was terminated in late March 2026 after Poolside's ~$2B raise failed to close; the site sits idle. A scaled-down ~400 MW revival with Google was mooted and those talks have gone quiet. The 2 GW figure remains the announced campus plan only; PAUSED removes it from the credible pipeline.

projects.name: Project Rainier
projects.description: AWS campus at New Carlisle, Indiana built for Anthropic training workloads on Trainium.
projects.analystNotes:
Reported at roughly 1 GW or more of IT power. IT load and site power are different quantities and the sources are not always explicit about which is meant.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: the prior 1,000 MW figure did not distinguish IT load from site power. Epoch estimates 910 MW IT operating (1,925 MW projected by Q1 2028); Amazon's own materials state 'more than 1 million Trainium2 chips' by end-2025, with Epoch estimating 1,045k. CNBC reports the full ~30-building site will draw more than 2.2 GW at completion.

projects.name: Prometheus Hyperscale Evanston
projects.analystNotes: 506-acre site on founder Trenton Thornock's family ranch; unanimous Uinta County conditional-use approval June 2026. 'Prometheus says construction will begin within six months of final permitting and take four to five years.' Mostly natural-gas powered, closed-loop water-glycol cooling. Capex null: reported $30B covers two Wyoming projects (Evanston plus a proposed Casper-area site), not this campus alone. Former BP CEO Bernard Looney leads the buildout. Some reports cite expansion potential to 5GW.

projects.name: QTS–Lancium Hall County
projects.analystNotes: Up to 11 QTS-built buildings on 465 acres at Lancium's Clean Campus; 'The site is supported by a 1GW grid connection.' On-site solar plus battery storage, closed-loop cooling; up to 7,000 peak construction jobs, ~350 permanent. No construction start or opening dates announced. Separate from Blackstone/QTS's $25B Pennsylvania commitment and the abandoned 2,100-acre Virginia Digital Gateway.

projects.name: Reliance Jamnagar AI Campus
projects.analystNotes: Media reports of up to 3 GW / 'world's largest' ambitions are unconfirmed by Reliance filings, so the 1 GW planned figure is used, basis unstated. A Meta–Reliance JV anchors a reported 168 MW lease at Jamnagar. A separate MOU for a twin 1 GW campus in Andhra Pradesh is MOU-stage and not recorded.

projects.name: SK Telecom Ulsan
projects.analystNotes: Groundbreaking Aug 2025; AWS anchor tenant. First phase 41 MW by Nov 2027, expanding to 103 MW by Feb 2029; basis unstated. The $5.88B figure is AWS's Korea-wide investment, so no site capex is recorded. SKT's July 2026 15 GW-by-2035 regional plan is aspirational and not recorded.

projects.name: Sakura Internet Ishikari
projects.analystNotes: ~2,000 H100s operational at Ishikari (NVIDIA PR: expanding 'from 2,000 to nearly 4,000 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs'); HGX B200 planned toward ~10,800 total GPUs. Company added ~1,100 Blackwell GPUs in a container DC at Ishikari announced 2026-02-24 (company announcement). Backed by ~JPY50.1bn METI subsidy for national GenAI compute; site targeted fully renewable by 2027. gpuCount reflects confirmed installed H100 base, not targets.

projects.name: Scala AI City (Phase 1)
projects.analystNotes: Aspirational full build is 4.75GW ('4.750MW distribuídos em mais de 7 milhões de metros quadrados') — among the largest DC ambitions in the Americas; MME granted a 5GW grid-reserve authorization, one of Brazil's largest ever. Only the 54MW/US$500M Phase 1 is committed; construction started after Eldorado do Sul enabling law was sanctioned. 100% renewable, PUE <=1.2 claimed, Malbec subsea-cable connectivity.

projects.name: SoftBank France Program
projects.analystNotes: Announced at Choose France 2026. Program across three sites (Loon-Plage/Dunkirk, Bosquel, Bouchain); capex is the USD equivalent of the up-to-€75B pledge, phase one €45B for 3.1 GW by 2031. Program-stage — no construction confirmed. Coordinates are the Loon-Plage lead site.

projects.name: SoftBank Sakai
projects.analystNotes: Conversion of Sharp's former Sakai LCD plant; over 150 MW initially with a stated path to over 400 MW. Capex is the property purchase (~$676M), not full fit-out. Original 2025 target slipped to 2026. Linked to the SB OpenAI Japan JV (Cristal Intelligence workloads).

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.description: Anchor site of the Stargate programme in Abilene, Texas, operated by Oracle with OpenAI as tenant.
projects.analystNotes:
Gas turbines rated up to ~300 MW are reported on site, bridging the gap while grid capacity is built.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: the previous 300 MW confirmed figure was Epoch's April total-facility-power estimate, which Epoch itself revised. Oracle stated 'In Abilene, 200MW is already operational' (April 2026) — that operator statement is what the confirmed column now carries. Epoch's live directory estimates 421 MW IT across Buildings 1–4 (May 2026), projecting 843 MW / all eight buildings by ~November 2026; recorded as a separate estimate. OpenAI capped the site at 1.2 GW in March 2026.

projects.name: Stargate Argentina
projects.analystNotes: Letter-of-intent stage: OpenAI and Sur Energy signed an LOI, up to $25B under Argentina's RIGI incentive regime. 'Up to 500 MW'; exact location and start date undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded.

projects.name: Stargate Doña Ana County
projects.description: Stargate site in Doña Ana County, New Mexico, announced by OpenAI with Oracle and SoftBank.
projects.analystNotes: Site confirmed by OpenAI's own announcement; no per-site capacity was published, so power is deliberately left blank rather than guessed.

projects.name: Stargate Korea — Jeollanam-do
projects.analystNotes: MOU stage only; exact site still being selected at announcement, so no coordinates are recorded. Shares the reported 20 MW combined initial capacity with the Samsung/Pohang site, so no per-site power claim is recorded.

projects.name: Stargate Korea — Pohang
projects.analystNotes: MOU/LOI stage only, signed 2025-10-01 during Altman's Seoul visit; no binding construction contract published. The reported 20 MW initial capacity is combined across both Korean sites, so no per-site power claim is recorded.

projects.name: Stargate Lordstown
projects.description: Stargate site at Lordstown, Ohio, announced by OpenAI with Oracle and SoftBank.
projects.analystNotes: Site confirmed by OpenAI; no per-site capacity published.

projects.name: Stargate Michigan
projects.analystNotes:
Developed by Related Digital for OpenAI/Oracle; DTE Energy supply plan approved at 1.4 GW (site power). The companies' own announcement says 'more than a gigawatt' of capacity. Groundbreaking held 2026-06-01. Capex ~$16B per press reports, not confirmed by the companies.

UPDATE 2026-08-01: capex was previously withheld because reports conflicted ($7B at announcement vs $16B later). Multiple outlets (CNBC at groundbreaking, Tom's Hardware, Manchester Mirror) now consistently report ~$16B; recorded at MEDIUM confidence. The $7B origin figure is retained here for the record.

projects.name: Stargate Milam County
projects.description: Stargate site in Milam County, Texas, announced by OpenAI with Oracle and SoftBank.
projects.analystNotes: Site confirmed by OpenAI; no per-site capacity published.

projects.name: Stargate Norway
projects.analystNotes: Nscale-Aker 50/50 JV, OpenAI offtaker; first European OpenAI-for-Countries site. Hydropower-fed. Capacity basis (IT vs site) not specified. The 100,000-GPU figure is a target, not a deployed count, recorded as an estimate, matching how other announced site targets are held. Both parties committed ~$1B to the initial 20 MW phase only.

projects.name: Stargate Shackelford County
projects.description: Vantage-developed Stargate site in Shackelford County, Texas — ten single-storey buildings across roughly 1,200 acres.
projects.analystNotes: 1.4 GW is stated as IT capacity, which is not the same as site power draw. Recorded as IT capacity and flagged, because the two are routinely conflated in reporting.

projects.name: Stargate UAE
projects.description: 1 GW compute cluster inside the UAE–US AI Campus in Abu Dhabi, built by G42 and operated with OpenAI and Oracle.
projects.analystNotes: The 1 GW cluster sits inside a wider 5 GW UAE–US AI Campus. Only the 1 GW cluster is counted here — counting the campus envelope as well would double-count the same megawatts.

projects.name: Stargate UK
projects.analystNotes: Announced Sept 2025; PAUSED April 2026 over UK energy costs and AI copyright rules, with no construction started. The 8,000/31,000 GPU figures were offtake exploration targets, never deployed, so no GPU claim is recorded. No MW figure was ever disclosed.

projects.name: Stargate Wisconsin
projects.analystNotes: One of the five Stargate sites announced 2025-09-23. 902 MW across four buildings per local reporting of the approved plan; Vantage's own words are 'close to a gigawatt of AI capacity' (IT). Site draw reported at 1.3 GW with later phases potentially to 3.5 GW. Groundbreaking Dec 2025, completion scheduled 2028.

projects.name: TELUS Sovereign AI Factory (Rimouski)
projects.analystNotes: Rimouski, QC facility operational Sept 2025 (NVIDIA Cloud Partner, HPE-built). May 2026: B.C. cluster announced — Kamloops expansion plus two Vancouver Westbank sites (M3 Mount Pleasant end-2026; 150 West Georgia 2029), >150MW/>60,000 GPUs by 2032 is a plan, not built. Quebec context: Hydro-Québec has restricted new >5MW data-centre allocations and proposed roughly doubling their rate (~13c/kWh) effective H2 2026 — a headwind for new Quebec builds. Power and GPU figures omitted on review: the Rimouski facility MW is undisclosed, and the >150 MW / 60,000-GPU figures are the 2032 British Columbia expansion plan, not built capacity.

projects.name: TeraWulf Justified
projects.analystNotes: Anthropic is the direct tenant on a 20-year lease (~$19B contracted revenue — revenue, not capex). Initial capacity H2 2027, full 401 MW critical IT load by early 2028. Part of Anthropic's US compute buildout alongside the Fluidstack program.

projects.name: TeraWulf Lake Mariner
projects.analystNotes: Former bitcoin mine on Lake Ontario converted to AI. Fluidstack leases total ~360 MW critical IT load; Google backstops ~$3.2B of Fluidstack obligations. Widely reported as the New York site of Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program, though Anthropic's announcement does not name Lake Mariner.

projects.name: Tesla Cortex
projects.analystNotes: Cortex 1 operational since 2024 at ~130 MW launch draw with 50,000 H100s shown; 500 MW is the stated full site-power target for the Cortex 2.0 expansion (reported mid-2026 completion). Larger 2026 GPU-count claims circulate only in weak sources and are not recorded.

projects.name: Ubilink.AI Supercomputing Center

location.city: Taipei (exact district not disclosed in cited sources)

projects.analystNotes: Billed as Taiwan's largest commercial AI supercomputing facility at launch (Nov 2024): 128 ASUS-built NVIDIA HGX H100 servers / 1,024 GPUs, 45.82 PFLOPS (TOP500 #31, Green500 #44), PUE 1.2, renewable-energy options via Shinfox. Partners state expansion toward ~10,240 H100/B100/B200 GPUs — plan, not installed. Distinct from the already-covered Foxconn/NVIDIA Kaohsiung AI factory. Caveat: coverage is company-announcement and Taiwanese trade press; limited Western trade-press verification, flagged per provenance rules.

projects.name: Volcano Cloud Taihang Phase II
projects.analystNotes: 4.5bn yuan (US$614m) campus in Guangling County Economic Development Zone Big Data Park, eastern Datong; 205,013 sqm, six two-storey DC buildings plus one six-storey integrated facility. SCMP reports 15,604 12kW server cabinets plus 510 network cabinets (implies ~187MW IT load, not stated as such — powerMw left null). Supports Doubao AI workloads; Datong ranked third nationally on CAICT computing-power index.

projects.name: Wonder Valley Phase 1

location.city: Greenview Industrial Gateway (south of Grande Prairie)

projects.analystNotes: Aspirational: developer pitches 7.5GW over 5-10 years and 'over $70 billion' lifetime investment, but as of Dec 2025 land purchase was not finalized, no new provincial permits filed, and construction is not expected before late 2028 (The Logic). 2026 earmarked for environmental/AUC permitting. Only Phase 1 (1.4GW, ~US$2B) recorded here; treat all capacity as unbuilt ambition. Recorded at the Phase 1 figure only; treat as unbuilt ambition per The Logic reporting.

projects.name: YTL Green Data Center Park
projects.analystNotes: 1,640-acre campus ~30 km from Singapore; 500 MW planned park capacity paired with a co-located 500 MW solar plant. Malaysia's first NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 AI datacenter (YTL AI Cloud) operational since Oct 2025; full park capacity not energized.

projects.name: Yiwu County AI Complex

compute.gpuModel: NVIDIA H100/H200 (planned per filings; sourcing unclear under export controls)

projects.analystNotes: AGGREGATE CAVEAT: the >115,000 Nvidia H100/H200 figure covers 39 data center projects approved in Q4 2024 across Xinjiang and Qinghai, per Bloomberg's review of filings — not one site. Bloomberg reports roughly 70% of planned compute is concentrated in this single government-backed complex near Yiwu (implying ~80k chips), powered by wind, solar and coal with free-electricity incentives. Chip sourcing path unverified; construction/tenders underway on 7 of 39 projects as of mid-2025.

projects.name: Z.ai Computing Centre

compute.gpuModel: Chinese domestic accelerators (vendor not named; Huawei Ascend implied)

projects.analystNotes: Facility in partial operation as of July 2026; 1GW figure is company-stated design capacity, IT-vs-site basis not specified. Site location not disclosed in Bloomberg/SCMP reporting — coordinates are Z.ai's Beijing HQ, not the DC. Z.ai has been on the US entity list since Jan 2025; also runs multiple 10,000+ chip clusters. GLM-5.2 reportedly trained entirely on Huawei Ascend. Coordinates omitted: the site location is undisclosed.

projects.name: eStruxture CAL-3
projects.analystNotes: Tier III design, up to 125kW/rack densities. CoreWeave signed as Phase 1 anchor tenant May 14, 2026 — its second Canadian site. eStruxture frames CAL-3 as part of 'more than C$1 billion' Alberta investment; capex here is the CA$750M (US$540M) CAL-3 figure.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 1
projects.analystNotes:
Original Colossus at the former Electrolux plant, operational since 2024. 300 MW is facility power consumption for the completed Phase 2 buildout, not on-site generation (the site separately has ~150 MW of Megapack buffering and gas turbines). 2026 reporting says Colossus 1 now serves inference while training moved to Colossus 2.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: the 300 MW previously shown as confirmed was Tom's Hardware's Phase 1+2 consumption target, wrongly attributed to a Musk statement that covered only the GPU count. Documented power: 150 MW grid interconnection energized May 2025 (MLGW/TVA), a further 150 MW approved February 2026 (energization unconfirmed), and ~247 MW of permitted on-site gas generation. The 230,000-GPU figure is primary (Musk, July 2025) and stands. Recent reporting has Colossus 1 shifted to inference duty.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 2
projects.description: Training cluster spanning Memphis, Tennessee and Southaven, Mississippi, generating power on site rather than waiting for utility interconnection.
projects.analystNotes:
On-site generation is the defining feature: the site sidesteps the interconnection queue, which is why its timeline is faster than grid-dependent peers.

CORRECTION 2026-08-01: the 2 GW figure is Musk's claimed total site capacity after the third-building purchase (Dec 2025), not current capacity — Epoch estimates 946 MW IT operating (Aug 2026), projecting 1,531 MW by Q1 2027. The prior 555k GPU figure was an Introl estimate; Musk's own statement was 550k GB200/GB300s as a first batch, and Epoch estimates ~440k Blackwell chips installed, which is now recorded.

projects.name: xAI MACROHARDRR
projects.analystNotes: Third Colossus-complex building, announced by Musk on X 2025-12-30; warehouse conversion under way through 2026. The ~2 GW figure is the stated target for the whole Memphis-area complex, not this building, so no power is recorded here.
